brief.question: How does HiBit Uninstaller's core uninstaller work (program list, columns, uninstall, leftover scan) so Tabula Rasa can rebuild only that part?
brief.purpose: Rebuild an uninstaller-only app named Tabula Rasa (Rust/egui)
brief.done_when: Registry sources, columns, uninstall flow and leftover scan rules are known with addresses.

findings.statement: Program list scanner (0x850e4c) reads HKLM 64-bit Uninstall, HKLM WOW6432Node Uninstall, then HKCU Uninstall (KEY_READ|WOW64_64KEY 0x20119). Entries need UninstallString; SystemComponent=1 or no DisplayName go to a separate hidden group. Size = EstimatedSize*1024, else InstallLocation folder size, else Unknown. WindowsInstaller=1 with {GUID} key → 'MsiExec.exe /X{GUID}'. Status bar shows item count and total size.
Before uninstalling (0x864758) the original checks whether another installed program shares the same install location and asks 'leftovers will... are you sure you want to continue' (Yes=6 proceeds).

handoff: Tabula Rasa (Rust/egui, workspace root) builds and passes checks. Program list rules from 0x850e4c, shared-folder warning from 0x864758 in MECHANICS.md/mechanics.json. Leftover scan is exact-name only, Recycle Bin + .reg backups. Open: original main window layout (no screenshot). Next ideas: export list, batch uninstall, quiet uninstall option.
